surface_verification.detail: Pure Python library/plugin change (file-locking primitives + retry predicate in shared/scripts/lib and plugins/shipwright-run/scripts/lib) with no dev_url, no web UI, no running server surface -- coverage is via the F0 pytest suite (554+38 unit/integration tests touching the diff directly, 96% diff-coverage) plus real-OS-primitive fidelity tests (msvcrt byte-range locks, cross-thread FileLock exclusion), not a browser/API/CLI-fixture surface.

behaviors.behavior: a byte-range-locked read (errno-only PermissionError, winerror=None) is retried and eventually succeeds — durable_read_text
a read still gives up loudly past the retry budget (not an infinite retry)
behaviors.evidence: test_atomic_write_read_winerror_none.py::test_read_text_still_gives_up_loudly_past_the_budget PASSED (deterministic fake clock, no real sleep)

behaviors.behavior: a None-winerror PermissionError with a DIFFERENT errno is not retried
the write-side retry path does not opt into None-winerror retrying (read-only fix)
a REAL msvcrt byte-range lock on this host is retried past, end-to-end
behaviors.evidence: test_atomic_write_read_winerror_none.py::test_real_byte_range_lock_is_retried_past PASSED (real OS primitive, Windows local + CI)

behaviors.behavior: _PhaseTasksLock delegates to the shared FileLock class instead of its own lock implementation
_PhaseTasksLock targets the canonical run_config_lock path (no re-derived local constant)
_PhaseTasksLock is bounded using the same timeout value as its run_config_lock sibling
same-thread nested acquisition enters immediately instead of self-deadlocking
every one of the 6 guarded lock-taking functions converts a LockTimeout into a retryable ok:false result
a holder via the sibling FileLock (run_config_lock) is waited out, not crashed into
a freeze_splits failure during apply_phase_result surfaces as ok:false instead of the design phase silently completing
